title: Ang 200–218: more Guru Arjan
hook: more short hymns of trust and the holy company

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ang 175: Guru Arjan's question about well-being, and two ways to read his answer. Today, his shorter hymns, and something that grows in the dark.

A chili seed is about the size of a freckle. You press it into the soil, cover it, water it, and then nothing happens. No signal, no progress bar. Bebe Jaswant, Simran's grandmother, grows chilies in old paint buckets along the back fence, and she never digs one up to check. When Simran, sore from a week of parallel parking, asked how she knows they're working, Bebe laughed: you don't know. You water.
screen: `A SEED THE SIZE OF A FRECKLE.` → `NO PROGRESS BAR.` → `YOU DON'T KNOW. YOU WATER.`

segments.voice: That's close to the word Guru Arjan keeps returning to in the short Gauri hymns from Ang 200 to 218: trust. Not a feeling you summon; a resting. One hymn in this stretch says, in paraphrase: the One who owns my body, mind and wealth is wise and knowing; He heard my sorrow and my joy, and my affairs came right; my soul trusts in the One alone. Notice what he trusts. Not the outcome. The One. And he doesn't say his sorrows stopped; he says they were heard. The other thread in these pages is the holy company, the sangat, the people you sing with. Trust comes easier in company, the way a seedling grows straighter tied to a stake. Here's the sense of it. Trust is something your hands know. A closed fist guards. An open palm can receive. At the gurdwara, karah prasad, the sweet offering, is received in cupped open hands. The body learns trust before the mind does. Bebe's buckets are her own small hymn: seed, soil, water, wait. She isn't careless; she waters every evening. Trust, on this path, isn't doing nothing. It's doing your part, and letting go of the part that was never yours.
screen: `TRUST: A RESTING, NOT A FEELING.` · `MY SOUL TRUSTS IN THE ONE.` · `EASIER IN COMPANY: THE SANGAT.` · `AN OPEN PALM CAN RECEIVE.` · then, large: `TRUST.`

segments.voice: Rest your hands in your lap and close them into loose fists; notice the small effort of holding on. Now slowly open them, palms up, and leave them open. Breathe there, and with each breath out, let your shoulders do what your hands just did.
Ang 200: more of Guru Arjan's short Gauri hymns, about trust and the holy company.
Your line: trust. Seed, soil, water, wait, and an open palm at the end of it. Sleep well.
